expects.query: Add the `warehouse_sample.mp4` sample video through NVStreamer so it becomes a live camera that the alerts pipeline can monitor, then start an alert on it for a ladder PPE violation — anyone on a ladder without a hardhat and safety vest — which is the condition the warehouse sample footage actually exhibits (see the alerts profile's `alert_type_config.json`), so the VLM reliably produces incidents. Onboard via the NVStreamer file-upload path (PUT the sample file to NVStreamer on port 31000) so the camera is NVStreamer-served, then register that NVStreamer RTSP in VIOS (port 30888) — even if a `warehouse_sample` entry already exists in VIOS, ensure it is the NVStreamer-served stream (re-onboard through NVStreamer if needed). Create the realtime alert rule by POSTing **directly** to Alert Bridge (`POST http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime`) — do NOT use the VSS Agent `/generate` endpoint and do NOT call the `rtvi-vlm` microservice on port 8018 directly. Registering the sensor in VIOS (POST /sensor/add) is REQUIRED — the task is NOT complete until `warehouse_sample` appears in VIOS. Before finishing, poll until ALL of these hold: NVStreamer (port 31000) lists `warehouse_sample`, VIOS (port 30888) lists `warehouse_sample`, AND rtvi-vlm (`http://localhost:8018/v1/streams/get-stream-info`) shows a live stream; wait and retry for a couple of minutes if any is still propagating.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi warehouse_sample && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (warehouse_sample is registered in VIOS; polls up to ~2 min to absorb VIOS registration/propagation delay).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:31000/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi warehouse_sample && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (warehouse_sample is served by the local NVStreamer instance on port 31000 - confirms onboarding via the NVStreamer file-ingest path, i.e. a file-backed sample stream rather than an arbitrary external camera; polls to absorb upload propagation).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 18 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:8018/v1/streams/get-stream-info 2>/dev/null | grep -qi rtsp && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (vss-rtvi-vlm has at least one registered live rtsp stream — confirms the alert rule was created and Alert Bridge wired the stream to rtvi-vlm; matches the rtsp scheme rather than a fixed port since the served URL is rewritten to the deployment's external IP, and polls up to ~4 min while the stream registers).

`sh -c 'curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime | python3 -c "import json,re,sys; rs=json.load(sys.stdin).get(\"rules\",[]); ok=[r for r in rs if re.match(r\"^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$\", str(r.get(\"sensor_id\") or \"\")) and str(r.get(\"sensor_name\") or \"\").lower().startswith(\"warehouse_sample\")]; sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (create-side identity contract: the stored rule carries the VIOS UUID in `sensor_id` and the human-readable sensor in `sensor_name` — the mirror image of the incidents query, which filters on the name. Deterministic end-state probe; it fails if a future change starts sending the name as `sensor_id` or drops `sensor_name`).

The trajectory created the rule by calling Alert Bridge `POST http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime` directly (payload carries the warehouse_sample RTSP `live_stream_url` and the ladder-PPE `prompt`) — it did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate`, and did NOT call the `rtvi-vlm` microservice (`:8018`) directly.

expects.query: List all sensors currently configured in VIOS.
checks: The trajectory issued a VIOS sensor-list call — `GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/list` on the VIOS ingress (`:30888`) OR the `vss-vios-sensor` service (`:30000`), either port is acceptable — not a direct database query and not via NVStreamer's port `31000`.

`curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array containing at least one sensor whose name references the warehouse sample (e.g. `warehouse_sample`, `warehouse_sample.mp4`, or similar) — confirms the prior NVStreamer onboarding propagated into VIOS.
The final assistant reply renders the sensor list as readable text/markdown including each sensor's name and state — not a raw response dump or an error trace.

expects.query:
Test fixture setup (this is harness setup, NOT an alerts-skill action): seed the incident store so the count queries in the NEXT TWO steps have known, non-empty data — four confirmed `fixture_intrusion` chunks for `warehouse_sample` (one 15 minutes old, then three spaced 30 s apart), one `fixture_other` chunk on the same sensor (a category decoy), and one decoy under a different sensor. The first line drops any fixture index left by an earlier run so the numbers are exact (200 = dropped, 404 = none to drop; anything else stops the seed). Run exactly:

ES=http://localhost:9200/mdx-vlm-incidents-fixture
code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -XDELETE "$ES"); case "$code" in 200|404) ;; *) echo "FIXTURE CLEANUP FAILED (HTTP $code) — STOP, do not seed"; exit 1;; esac
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
iso() { date -u -d "@$1" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }
seed() { curl -sf -XPUT "$ES/_doc/fixture-$1-$3?refresh=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"sensorId\":\"$1\",\"category\":\"${4:-fixture_intrusion}\",\"timestamp\":\"$(iso $2)\",\"end\":\"$(iso $(($2+10)))\",\"description\":\"seeded fixture chunk for $1\",\"info\":{\"verdict\":\"confirmed\",\"chunkIdx\":\"$3\"}}" && echo || { echo "SEED FAILED for $1 chunk $3 — Elasticsearch unreachable or rejected the document; STOP"; return 1; }; }
seed warehouse_sample $((NOW-900)) 0 \
  && seed warehouse_sample $((NOW-60)) 4 \
  && seed warehouse_sample $((NOW-30)) 5 \
  && seed warehouse_sample "$NOW" 6 \
  && seed warehouse_sample "$NOW" 9 fixture_other \
  && seed cam_decoy "$NOW" 0 \
  || { echo "FIXTURE INCOMPLETE — STOP, do not proceed to the next step"; exit 1; }

All six must return Elasticsearch "result":"created" (the seeds are chained, so the first failure stops the rest). If :9200 is unreachable or any seed fails, say so and STOP — do not proceed. The fixture stays in the store for the following steps; its categories (`fixture_*`) are unique to this spec.
checks: The trajectory deleted the `mdx-vlm-incidents-fixture` index (HTTP 200, or 404 when none existed) and then PUT six incident documents into it (`http://localhost:9200/mdx-vlm-incidents-fixture/_doc/fixture-<sensor>-<idx>`) with `refresh=true`: four `sensorId: warehouse_sample` / `category: fixture_intrusion`, one `sensorId: warehouse_sample` / `category: fixture_other` (the category decoy), and one under a DIFFERENT `sensorId` (the sensor decoy), each with `info.verdict: confirmed`, an ISO-8601 `timestamp` and `end`, and a string `info.chunkIdx`. Elasticsearch returned `"result": "created"` for each — the incident store now holds exactly five warehouse_sample fixture chunks plus one other-sensor chunk.

A verification confirms the fixture is queryable: `curl -sf 'http://localhost:9200/mdx-vlm-incidents-*/_count' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":{"term":{"sensorId.keyword":"warehouse_sample"}}}'` returns `count >= 5`, and the store-wide `_count` is strictly greater (it includes the decoy).

`curl -sf 'http://localhost:9200/mdx-vlm-incidents-fixture/_count' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":{"range":{"timestamp":{"gte":"now-1d"}}}}' | python3 -c "import json,sys; sys.exit(0 if json.load(sys.stdin)['count']==6 else 1)"` returns exit 0 (the six fixture documents carry parseable `timestamp` values inside the last day — a malformed or empty timestamp would be invisible to the incidents endpoint's range filter and sort).

expects.query: How many incidents has the alert recorded for the warehouse sample sensor? Query Alert Bridge directly — `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` (scope the query to that sensor). Report the count. Do NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` endpoint.
checks: The trajectory queried incidents by calling Alert Bridge `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` directly (optionally scoped with `?sensor_id=<sensor name>`). It did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate`, and did not answer the count from memory.

The incidents response captured in the trajectory is a well-formed `IncidentListResponse` (HTTP 200, top-level `status`, an `incidents` array, integer `count`/`total`, `timestamp`), and the count the agent reports is grounded in that payload. The figure is the response's `total`, the number of matching documents; the page-size `count` (or the length of `incidents`) only qualifies while it equals `total`, since past that it reports the page rather than the result. Because the fixture step seeded five warehouse_sample incidents, a correctly name-scoped query returns `total >= 5`; a reported 0 now signals a scoping error (an undeclared query param, a UUID identity, or an empty-store misread), not an empty store.

The final assistant reply reports a numeric incident count for the warehouse sample sensor that equals the name-scoped `total` (>= 5, since the fixture seeded five warehouse_sample incidents) — not 0, and not the store-wide total — not an error trace and not raw JSON.

Sensor scoping, when used, passes the sensor NAME: if the trajectory filters the incident query with `?sensor_id=...`, the value is the sensor name as stored in the incident documents' `sensorId` field (e.g. `warehouse_sample`) — NOT a VIOS UUID. The endpoint term-matches that field, so a UUID silently returns `count: 0`, which is indistinguishable from an empty store. A UUID-scoped query against `/api/v1/realtime/incidents` is wrong when it stands in for the name query: reporting 'none found' with no name-scoped query behind it is a failure. The follow-up is not optional: when the name query comes back zero, the trajectory must also show a query scoped to the sensor's VIOS UUID before any 'none found' is reported, because a zero under one identity is not yet an answer. That sequence — name first, UUID only after it returned zero — is the skill's documented alternate-identity check and passes. The follow-up may only be missing if the trajectory shows VIOS could not be reached to resolve the UUID. The number reported has to be the one that was found: if the name query came back zero and the UUID query did not, the reply reports the UUID result and names that identity — a reply that still says zero fails. Crediting either identity is only free when both came back zero. None of this applies to rule creation, where the payload's `sensor_id` must be the VIOS UUID — step 2 checks that separately. The count reported must also be scoped to warehouse_sample: either the request filtered server-side by name, or the agent fetched the unfiltered list and counted only the documents whose `sensorId` is that sensor — the latter only counts as correct when the response was complete (`count` equals `total`), since a truncated page yields a partial figure indistinguishable from a full one. Answering a sensor-specific question with a bare global `count`/`total` over every sensor in the store is a failure. The seeded fixture makes this gradable on the NUMBER, not the wording: five incidents carry `sensorId: warehouse_sample` and at least one other carries a different sensorId, so a correct name-scoped query returns the warehouse_sample `total` (>= 5), a `?sensor=`/undeclared-param or unscoped query returns the strictly-LARGER store-wide total (it includes the decoy), and a VIOS-UUID-scoped query returns 0. The reported number MUST equal the name-scoped total and MUST be strictly less than the store-wide total — reporting the global total, or a UUID-scoped 0, fails on the number.

The ask names NO period, so the query stays in the raw view: no request in this step carries `consolidate=true`. The consolidated view needs a bounded `start_time`/`end_time` window (Alert Bridge answers HTTP 400 without one) and counts EVENTS, not chunks — the fixture's five warehouse_sample chunks alone fold into three events (plus any live ladder-PPE events from step 2) — so a consolidated answer here reports a small event count where the question asked how many incident records exist (>= 5). Inventing a window to make `consolidate=true` work, or reporting the event count as the incident count, fails. (The next step asks the event question on purpose.)

expects.query: Over the last 24 hours, how many separate `fixture_intrusion` events did the alert record on the warehouse sample sensor? Query Alert Bridge directly — `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` — and report the number of events, not the number of raw chunk documents. Do NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` endpoint.
checks: The trajectory answered from the consolidated view: a `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` carrying `consolidate=true` together with BOTH `start_time` and `end_time` as real ISO-8601 UTC values spanning roughly the last 24 hours (the end bound at or after the fixture step's seeding time, the start bound before it), scoped with `sensor_id=warehouse_sample` (the sensor NAME as stored in `sensorId`, not a VIOS UUID) and `category=fixture_intrusion` (the ask named the category). It did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` and did not answer the count from memory.

The number the agent reports is the consolidated response's `total`, and it equals 2. The fixture seeded four confirmed `fixture_intrusion` chunks on warehouse_sample — one 15 minutes older than a cluster of three spaced 30 s apart — and the deployment ships the default `rtvi_vlm.consolidation.max_inter_alert_gap_seconds: 60`, so the window holds exactly two consolidated `fixture_intrusion` events (the category is unique to the fixture, so no live RT-VLM incident can join them). The fixture also seeded one `fixture_other` chunk on the same sensor, and the live ladder-PPE rule from step 2 may have written confirmed chunks on it too: a consolidated query that omits `category=` therefore returns at least 3 (2 + the decoy + any live events), so a reported number that equals that category-less total means the category filter was dropped. Reporting the raw `total` (>= 5) or a raw page's `count` means the raw view was used; a store-wide figure means the decoy leaked in (unscoped, or an undeclared `?sensor=`-style param); 0 means UUID scoping or a mis-copied category. If Alert Bridge answered HTTP 400 `validation_failed` at any point, the trajectory treated it as a missing time window and re-issued the query with both bounds — it did not fall back to the unfiltered `/incidents` list, did not report Alert Bridge as unreachable, and did not report 0.

The final assistant reply states 2 `fixture_intrusion` events for the warehouse sample sensor (it may add that they span 4 chunks) and names the window it covers, as readable text — not raw JSON and not an error trace. It does NOT present 4 (the chunk count) or the category-less event total (3 or more, which includes the `fixture_other` decoy) as the number of events.

`sh -c 'curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_intrusion --data-urlencode "start_time=$(date -u -d "-1 day" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --data-urlencode "end_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --data-urlencode consolidate=true | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); ev=r[\"incidents\"]; sys.exit(0 if r[\"total\"]==2 and r.get(\"truncated\") is False and len(ev)==2 and all(e[\"info\"].get(\"isConsolidated\")==\"true\" for e in ev) and sorted(int(e[\"info\"][\"chunkCount\"]) for e in ev)==[1,3] else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (deterministic contract probe of the consolidated view over the seeded fixture: two events, `truncated: false`, chunk counts 1 and 3, every event flagged `info.isConsolidated`).

`sh -c 'S=$(date -u -d "-1 day" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); E=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_other --data-urlencode consolidate=true --data-urlencode limit=1000 --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode "end_time=$E" | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); sys.exit(0 if r[\"total\"]==1 and r[\"incidents\"][0][\"info\"][\"chunkCount\"]==\"1\" else 1)" && curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode consolidate=true --data-urlencode limit=1000 --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode "end_time=$E" | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); cats={e[\"category\"] for e in r[\"incidents\"]}; sys.exit(0 if r[\"total\"]>=3 and {\"fixture_intrusion\",\"fixture_other\"} <= cats else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (deterministic decoy probe: `category=fixture_other` alone folds to exactly one single-chunk event, and the same window with no category holds at least 3 events spanning both fixture categories — the live ladder-PPE rule from step 2 may add more, so the category-less total is a floor, not an exact value; the graded 2 is only reachable with `category=fixture_intrusion`).

`sh -c 'r=$(curl -s --max-time 15 -w "\n%{http_code}" "http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents?consolidate=true&sensor_id=warehouse_sample"); case "$r" in *validation_failed*400) exit 0;; esac; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (deterministic negative probe: `consolidate=true` without a time window is rejected with HTTP 400 `validation_failed`, the case the skill tells the agent to fix rather than treat as an outage).
